$comment: review-manifest.json — the single source of truth for every quality gate in this repo.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
The repo already had excellent gates. The failure mode was never 'no gate' — it was
'a gate nobody runs'. Measured on 2026-09-15: seven gates were referenced by ZERO
workflows, `ci:quality` and `ci:predeploy` (the composite local scripts) were referenced
by zero workflows too, and the review checklist named a `lint` gate that did not exist at
all. Every one of those looked like protection and provided none.
REMOVED 2026-09-16: the `ci:predeploy` composite is gone, and so is every `runs[]`
entry that cited it. Nothing invoked it (`grep -rn "npm run ci:predeploy"` found no
caller outside its own definition), so a gate listing it was claiming a run location
that did not exist -- and `runs[]` is what C3 reads to answer "is every blocking gate
run somewhere". Its gates are inlined in both deploy workflows, one step per gate,
which is also what rule 7 requires. `ci:predeploy:local` stays: it is a documented
local convenience and it never claimed to run in CI.
A gate that exists but does not run is worse than no gate: it produces false confidence,
and it teaches reviewers that the checklist is aspirational. So the inventory is now data,
and scripts/ci/verify-review-manifest.mjs asserts it against reality.
FIELDS
script    the package.json script name. Must exist, or the manifest gate fails.
tier      0 = machine-checkable, must be green before review
1 = deploy/operability gate, required on the shipping path
2 = measured, report-only, never blocks
blocking  true = a failure must stop the change. A blocking gate with an empty `runs`
array is a manifest error and fails the manifest gate.
provenBy  the mutation battery that demonstrates this gate CAN fail, or null.
null is honest, not shameful: it records 'hypothesis, not proof'. The manifest
gate reports the count so the gap is visible instead of assumed away.
battery   what kind of mutation battery exists, if any. This field is what makes
`verify:batteries` possible: the runner READS it instead of repeating a
hand-typed list, so the set cannot drift from this classification.
"ci"    hermetic — no credentials, no server, no database. Runs in CI
on every PR via `npm run verify:batteries`.
"infra" needs a live Postgres, the Supabase transport, or a real HTTP
server to be meaningful, so it does NOT run on every PR.
"none"  no battery exists.
Added 2026-09-15, together with the runner. Before it, `provenBy` said a
battery EXISTED but nothing said whether it could RUN anywhere — which is
how 22 batteries came to be cited in a manifest that no workflow executed.
runs      every place this gate is actually invoked. 'ci.yml#job' = a GitHub job.
'review:gate' = the local pre-push gate. A gate listed ONLY under review:gate
is local-only: CI does not back it, which is a fact a reviewer needs.
ADDED 2026-09-16: the four e2e guards. They were in NO manifest entry while the
`e2e` job ran them, and three of their batteries had no caller at all -- so the
one job whose gates the inventory did not know about was also the one where
"proven able to fail" was quietly decaying. e2e:public has no battery and is
recorded as a hypothesis (provenBy: null) rather than left unlisted.

gates.note: The original ratchet, and the idiom lint-ratchet.mjs copies: fail only on NEW debt, so the pipeline is never permanently red. Baseline was already 0 errors on 2026-09-03, so the ratchet currently enforces a clean tree — which also means no real edit can exercise its 'count increased' path, so the battery plants one deliberate type error in a temp file it removes afterwards. Proven 2026-09-15: 5 killed / 0 survived, covering both failure conditions plus the exit-2 tooling path, with the real baseline never written to.

gates.note: Wired into ci.yml#quality-gates on 2026-09-15. Before that it ran only via ci:quality, an npm script no workflow references, so CI never typechecked the indexer at all. Proven 2026-09-15 by typecheck-indexer.mutations.sh: 1 killed / 0 survived / 4 ok-green. This is the thinnest gate in the manifest — tsc does the checking and package.json adds no logic — so the battery proves the part that CAN regress: the include list deciding scope. Measured: removing indexer/src/**/*.ts from include drops the checked set from 37 files to 1 and the gate still exits 0. tsc is behaving correctly (one clean file really has no type errors) and there is nothing to fix; what is asserted is that the scope matches its pinned count, so a future narrowing trips a test instead of passing quietly. T5 demonstrates that assertion can fail by narrowing include in a fixture config. T3 pins the documented separation: tsconfig.indexer.json must not extend the app tsconfig nor reach src/** or netlify/** — indexer code must never leak into npm run typecheck. T1/T2 are the error/control pair.

gates.note: Proven 2026-09-15 by boundary.mutations.sh: 5 killed / 0 survived / 6 ok-green. The load-bearing result is SEVERITY handling in both directions: an error-severity violation exits 1, and the IDENTICAL violation demoted to warn exits 0 (B1/B1b), plus a warn-severity violation exiting 0 and the same one raised to error exiting 1 (B2/B2b). Without both pairs the gate could either fail on every violation — making the warn rule unshippable — or ignore severity and silently demote the kernel rule. Also pins the contexts-no-cross-context pathNot exemption: reaching another context internal.ts is a violation, reaching its service.ts is the documented owner-interface pattern and must stay green. The rule SET itself is owned by indexer/src/boundary.test.ts (6 rules + depcruise oracle); this battery owns the CLI exit code that ci:quality consumes.
gates.batteryNote: Hermetic: no credentials, no server, no database. Runs in CI on every PR via `npm run verify:batteries`.

gates.note: A-07 RESOLVED 2026-09-17. This is NOT a competing gate. `boundary` is authoritative: it is wired into ci.yml#boundary, it is blocking, it has a mutation battery, and it owns the 6 rules. This entry is the REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION that `boundary.ts` mirrors by hand against the same .dependency-cruiser.cjs — which is exactly why it must be RUN, not merely present. The binary is now genuinely executed as an oracle by indexer/src/boundary.test.ts, a test that had been named 'matches the depcruise oracle' since it was written while never invoking it (it re-derived the verdict from boundary.ts and asserted the same 0). Measured on this tree 2026-09-17: exit 0 in ~6 s, 210 modules / 648 dependencies cruised. It stays non-blocking deliberately — a second blocking gate over the same config would be redundant, and the drift it can actually catch is a drift in boundary.ts's hand-mirroring, which is caught where the mirroring lives.
gates.batteryNote: No mutation battery, and none is wanted. This is not a gate; it is the oracle that boundary.test.ts pins itself against. That it can fail is not in question — it exits non-zero on a violation by construction — and a battery here would be testing dependency-cruiser rather than this repository. The gate that needs proving is `boundary`, and boundary.mutations.sh proves it (5 killed / 0 survived / 6 ok-green).

gates.note: Three documents claimed universal edge validation (ARCHITECTURE.md "Zod validation at API edge", ENGINEERING_PLAYBOOK.md "Already the pattern; keep it", CODE_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md "All input validated by a Zod schema at the handler edge"). Measured 2026-09-16: validatePayload() had 7 call sites, ALL of them in surfaces/auth.ts, against 81 routed actions — and the jobs surface handed four unknown-typed arguments straight to Postgres TEXT columns. This gate makes the claim measurable. TWO MECHANISMS COUNT, and the second exists for a measured reason: importing zod (validate.ts) into contexts/jobs and contexts/applications added ~67 KB to EIGHT entry points and pushed files.js over the 600 KB hard ceiling (555.3 -> 622.6 KB), because contexts/applications is imported by master-data, registry and _lib/ai/cv — one zod import in a shared context leaks the library into most of the deployment. So the narrow entries use _lib/kernel/guard.ts instead: dependency-free, ~5 KB (jobs.js +4.8 KB, mail.js +6.0 KB, both inside the 8 KB floor). A gate that recognised only zod would push the next contributor back into that regression. It is a ratchet, not a hard rule: the unvalidated set is frozen in .ci/validation-baseline.json and may only shrink, so a new unvalidated write fails AND a baseline entry that has since been validated also fails (a baseline that cannot shrink stops describing reality). Coverage at introduction: 9/33 mutating actions. Battery proven 2026-09-16: 6 killed / 0 survived / 1 ok-green, each asserted on its EXACT exit code rather than merely non-zero — D1 a write losing its validation, D2 an action newly declared mutating with no schema, D3 stale baseline, D4 vanished baseline entry, V1 an empty MUTATING set (exit 2), V2 an unresolvable action (exit 2) — plus R1, which proves the remedy printed in the failure message actually resolves D3. The exit-code distinction is load-bearing: exit 1 means the gate judged a violation, exit 2 means it could not judge at all, and the first draft of D2 passed by tripping the tooling guard while claiming to cover the new-debt rule.

gates.note: The workflow files as GitHub reads them. Added 2026-09-17 after the repository was measured at 32 failed runs and ZERO successful ones, every run with no jobs: _notify.yml used `secrets` in a step-level `if:`, which GitHub rejects by refusing the WHOLE FILE ("Unrecognized named-value: secrets"), and a called workflow that will not parse takes its callers down with it — so ci.yml, deploy-staging.yml, deploy-production.yml and rollback.yml were all dead at once, and the automatic post-deploy rollback had never been armed. Nothing local could see it: every existing gate tests the code, and none of them reads the workflows as GitHub does. Rules: W1 shape · W2 no secrets in if: · W3 callable targets · W4 non-empty name (GitHub reports the FILE PATH as the name when a workflow will not parse — that is the tell that found this).

gates.note:
The vitest `indexer` project (14 files) runs only via ci:quality, which no workflow calls — so CI never runs it. See audit A-06. Proven 2026-09-15 by test.mutations.sh: 3 killed / 0 survived / 3 ok-green. This gate has no script of its own — `vitest run` IS the gate — so the battery proves the RUNNER CONTRACT rather than mutation-testing a checker: a failing test exits non-zero (X1, and X3 in the backend project so neither project can be silently dropped), a passing test goes green (X2, ruling out an always-failing runner), both projects are discoverable by the names the CI workflow uses (X6), and the include globs are intact (X5). The decisive case is X4: narrowing the frontend include to a non-existent path makes vitest refuse with "No test files found, exiting with code 1" rather than reporting success over an empty suite. That is the vacuous-pass defect class found three times elsewhere today, and here the runner gets it RIGHT — no fix follows, and the file says so. Scope is stated honestly: this proves the runner and the structure, NOT that the assertions inside the 140 test files are meaningful.
SECOND BATTERY ADDED 2026-09-16: settings-limit.mutations.sh (7 killed / 0 survived / 1 ok-green), covering netlify/functions/_lib/db/settings-limit.test.ts — the OTHER call site of the limit=1 bug this entry already guards via jobs-limit.test.ts. findSettings()/findAnnouncements() inherited findTable()'s default of limit=1; measured against the live database, sys_config holds 158 rows and the single row read was config_type="tsk", so loadPublicBase() built dropdowns={tsk:['TSK VIBE']} and every other key was ABSENT — reported by the owner as "ga ada drop downnya". replaceConfigItems() resolves its DELETE set through the same function, so editing a list removed one row and reinserted the whole list: measured production signature, tsk 36 rows / 35 distinct values ('TSK MAHER' twice). TWO DEFECTS IN THE PROOF ITSELF were found by executing it, both of the kind that make a battery lie: M1 SURVIVED the first run because the guard regex used [\s\S]*? unscoped to the function body, so when findSettings() lost its limit the pattern matched the limit belonging to findAnnouncements() — an aggregate match reporting a pass over a body that no longer passed anything; and the battery's own restore check reported all three borrowed files as changed twice over (it compared after deleting its own snapshots, and read node argv[2] under  where arguments start at argv[1]). Baseline is snapshotted from the LIVE tree, not git HEAD, because HEAD holds pre-fix bytes.

gates.note:
This file's own gate. Asserts every named gate exists, is run somewhere, and that the review docs name no gate that does not exist. Wired into ci.yml#quality-gates on 2026-09-15, so CI now enforces the inventory it is part of. Battery extended to 11 mutations on 2026-09-15 to cover C6 (the new check that a `runs` workflow claim is true): S8 — claiming a gate runs in a real job that does not invoke it — SURVIVED the first C6 implementation, because it searched the whole workflow file rather than the job block, so it verified 'runs somewhere in this file' instead of the actual per-job claim. C6 was scoped to the job's own block and S8 now dies. 11 killed / 0 survived.
SECOND FINDING, 2026-09-15, FOUND BY RUNNING IT: this battery ABORTED at S3 — six of its eleven mutations could never fire. S3, S6, S7, S8 and S9 were anchored on `"runs": ["ci.yml#classes", "ci:quality", "review:gate"]` as a ONE-LINE string; review-manifest.json has always stored `runs` as a multi-line array, so `mut` matched nothing and the battery refused to continue (its guard working correctly — it aborted rather than reporting a phantom verdict). S6-S9 were additionally anchored on verify:md's `note` PROSE, which is rewritten whenever that gate's story changes. All six were rewritten to mutate the PARSED JSON STRUCTURE (`json_mut`, addressing a gate by name) instead of raw text, so reformatting the manifest or rewording a note can no longer kill them. Result: 11 killed / 0 survived / 1 ok-green, where before the run died at case 3. NOTE THE SHAPE OF THIS DEFECT: the battery was committed, cited here, and green on paper for as long as nobody executed it. Nothing about the GATE was broken. The proof had rotted, and a rotted proof is indistinguishable from a hole until someone re-runs it — which is the entire argument for `verify:batteries`.
gates.batteryNote: Hermetic: no credentials, no server, no database. Runs in CI on every PR via `npm run verify:batteries`.

gates.note: THE GATE THAT CLOSES THE LARGEST GAP IN THIS FILE. Until 2026-09-15 the manifest printed 'proven able to fail 22/22 (100%)' while nothing ran a single battery: `grep -c 'mutations\.sh' .github/workflows/*.yml` returned one hit, and that hit is a COMMENT in ci.yml line 68, not a `run:`. No npm script invoked them either. So the number meant "was once observed to fail", never "still does" — and the decay is not hypothetical. On its first run this runner found that `check-md-tables.mutations.sh` had a DEAD mutation: its anchored prose had been rewritten upstream, so its `str.replace()` matched nothing, wrote the file back unchanged, and the gate stayed correctly green while the battery reported SURVIVED. A dead mutation and a hole in a gate look identical from the outside; only re-running tells them apart. This gate runs the 17 hermetic batteries and fails when any one stops discriminating. It does NOT prove the 6 infra batteries or the 1 battery-less gate — the runner prints that remainder explicitly so a green run is never read as total proof.
gates.batteryNote: Hermetic. This battery breaks the runner/battery recursion by invoking the runner with `--only=verify:md`, which restricts it to one cheap battery that is not this one.

gates.note: Wired onto the shipping path 2026-09-15. Staging runs it without --strict; production runs `--profile production --strict`. Proven 2026-09-15 by verify-env.mutations.sh: 8 killed / 0 survived / 7 ok-green. The battery is offline-only because the gate reads process.env rather than a file: it hides .env.local/.env.lokal for the duration so the measured environment is exactly the one each case exports. That matters — applyEnvFiles() treats an EMPTY string as unset, so the obvious probe (`PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL= node …`) is refilled from .env.local and reports a green run that looks identical to a gate which cannot fail. Tier stays 1 because the runner still needs credentials to be meaningful, but the VERDICT logic is fully proven offline.

gates.note: The database is migrated by hand, so it can be behind the code. When it is, PostgREST answers 200 with an empty result and the app degrades silently. Both deploy workflows gate on it before publishing; the staging run carries an emergency `skip-db-gate` input for manual dispatches only, which the normal path never takes. PROVEN 2026-09-15: 7 killed / 0 survived / 4 ok-green against a local PostgREST stand-in. Offline-provable because its TRANSPORT is a base URL: `--contract` redirects the check, and `SUPABASE_URL` + a dummy key redirect the transport, so the verdict logic is exercised without touching the real database. The battery drives the whole verdict path, including D3 vs D3b — the SAME absent table exits 1 as `required` and 0 as `optional`, so severity is proven to decide rather than being assumed. SEE ALSO the operational note below. OPERATIONAL, MEASURED 2026-09-15: `npm run verify:db` from a developer machine CONNECTS TO THE LIVE PRODUCTION SUPABASE DATABASE. The gate calls applyEnvFiles() internally, which loads SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY from .env.local, so an `env SUPABASE_URL=... node gate` assignment cannot withhold them (an empty string counts as unset and is refilled; measured: 23 variables loaded, 8 SUPABASE ones). Running it unconfigured reports `DATABASE CONTRACT OK` against production and exits 0. This is intended for CI, where the credential comes from the GitHub Environment; locally it is a production-touching read. The battery is therefore hermetic by MOVING the env files aside for the whole run, and says so in its header.

gates.note: MOVED 2026-09-15: was briefly declared under ci.yml#quality-gates; C6 caught that the claim was false the moment it was written — verify:schema reads the live database, and CI has no database credential. The right home is the deploy path, where the credential exists: it now runs in both deploy workflows immediately before the RLS gate. schema.generated.ts is the typed view of the live DB, and a stale one makes every query compile against a schema that no longer exists — silently, because PostgREST answers 200 with an empty result. PROVEN 2026-09-15: 6 killed / 0 survived / 4 ok-green against a local PostgREST stand-in. Offline-provable for the same reason as verify:db — the TRANSPORT is a base URL, not the check. The decisive pair is S2 (a column added upstream is DRIFT, exit 1) against S1 (a committed file matching the live render passes, exit 0): the same gate, the same stand-in, one difference, so the drift verdict is proven to decide rather than assumed. S7 pins the case that a rename-free REORDER is still drift, which a name-set comparison alone would miss; S5 proves an empty stand-in is refused (exit 2) instead of being written out as a zero-table schema, and S5b proves that refusal says why. Fail-closed on missing/wrong credentials is S3/S4/S6. S8 checks the refusal reports both digests and the fix command. NO FALSE ALARM: this battery also documents, and then measures, a defect in the batteries themselves — see the pre-existing-dirty snapshot note in the three batteries dated 2026-09-15.

gates.note:
NOT PROVEN, and deliberately left that way on 2026-09-15. It needs live credentials: with none it exits 2 on every path, and the only local substitute is stubbing `pg`/PostgREST, which would prove the verdict logic while leaving the SQL — the actual check — untested. A battery that certifies the wrong half is worse than none, so this stays an open gap until it can run against a disposable Postgres in CI. MEASURED GAP, NOW CLOSED (2026-09-15): this gate used to be on NO shipping path — invoked only from ci:predeploy, which no workflow referenced, with no workflow supplying SUPABASE_DB_URL, so neither its decisive mode nor the gate itself ran before production shipped and migrations/012_rls_lockdown.sql was unprotected on the path that deploys. It is now a blocking step in both deploy workflows, immediately after the database contract gate, and both supply SUPABASE_DB_URL to select the DEFINITIVE catalog mode. This is the asymmetric gate: an application rollback does NOT restore table privileges, so a policy that drifts open cannot be undone by rolling back the deploy.
PROVEN 2026-09-15: 7 killed / 0 survived / 2 ok-green against a REAL PostgreSQL 18.4
(the devDependency embedded-postgres ships genuine initdb/postgres binaries), so the
catalog SQL itself is exercised, not a stub. THE PREVIOUS NOTE IN THIS ENTRY WAS WRONG,
and the correction is the point: it said this gate "needs live credentials" and could only
be proven by stubbing pg, which "would prove the verdict logic while leaving the SQL — the
actual check — untested". Measured: the gate runs locally with no extra credentials because
initDbEnv() composes SUPABASE_DB_URL from Direct_Connection_DB in .env.local, and a local
throwaway cluster replaces the transport while the CHECK runs unchanged. One supporting
change to the gate was required — honouring libpq PGSSLMODE, because a local cluster has no
TLS and the gate hard-coded `ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false }`.

A REAL DEFECT WAS FOUND WHILE PROVING. The third check — "a policy granted to PUBLIC with
USING (true)" — could never fire for the incident that motivated the gate. It queried
`polqual is null`, but Postgres stores a written `USING (true)` as the EXPRESSION 'true',
never NULL, so the query returned zero rows for exactly the shape
migrations/012_rls_lockdown.sql:76-79 describes ("`USING (true)` on a FOR ALL policy, granted
to PUBLIC"). Only a policy with no USING clause at all matched. Fixed in the same commit;
case R5 is that incident reintroduced, and it SURVIVED against the old predicate and is
KILLED against the new one — the falsification, not merely a green run. R5b is the paired
control: the RESTRICTIVE PUBLIC policy shape all three of the live database's real policies
use must stay GREEN, or the check would have to be disabled and every other guard would go
with it.

gates.note: The gate whose verdict can trigger netlify-rollback.mjs, so both error directions are expensive: too strict rolls production back over an unwired HEALTH_TOKEN, too lenient ships the outage. PROVEN 2026-09-15: 8 killed / 0 survived / 4 ok-green. Scope is the CLI exit-code contract — `checkUrl`/`classifyHealth` are already pinned by 20 tests in netlify/functions/_lib/smoke-test-health.test.ts, which imports the module specifically so main() never runs; that file therefore never reaches the exit code the workflows actually consume, and this battery does. The false-alarm surface is pinned by a three-case chain that varies ONE thing at a time: S7 (503 + `HEALTH_TOKEN is not configured` body, no token) must stay GREEN and warn; S7b (same 503, same absent token, body WITHOUT the marker) must exit 1 — this is what stops S7 from being satisfiable by a gate that special-cases every 503; S8 (same marker body as S7, token now supplied) must exit 1 — this is what stops the deliberate asymmetry from hiding a real outage from the rollback trigger. An earlier S7 sent a body without the marker and reported UNEXPECTED exit=1; the gate was right and the fixture was wrong, and S8 was worthless until the chain was fixed.

gates.note: Every rendered <label> must be tied to its control (a `for=` that resolves, or wrapping the control) — invisible in the source, because these forms build their labels inside helper components and `.map()` loops, where ONE source line renders 55 labels. MEASURED 2026-09-16 on the built artifact, before the fix: 4 of 23 associated on /master, 0 of 9 on /apply, 0 of 12 on /siswa-baru. After: 219 of 219 rendered labels across FOUR routes (/master 5 screens 130, /apply 9, /siswa-baru 12, /ai-cv 68), plus 3 group labels that `for=` cannot express at all and that are now `<fieldset>`+`<legend>`. `noLabelWithoutControl` moved only 138 -> 95, and that gap is the point — the rule counts SOURCE LOCATIONS, the user meets rendered labels. The guard catches the three ways this wiring rots silently: a `for=` pointing at a non-existent id, the SAME id emitted twice (so `for=` resolves to the wrong control), and a group that has lost its accessible name. Runs in the `e2e` job, which is gated on `push` (or an explicit `run-e2e` input) rather than every PR — so on a pull request this gate is NOT enforced. That is recorded here because a reviewer reading `runs` deserves to know CI does not back it before the merge.
gates.batteryNote: Needs a real HTTP server, so it is classified `infra` alongside its four e2e siblings and is deliberately NOT executed by `verify:batteries`. It needs NO backend: it builds, starts its own `astro preview` on a port it owns, and drives Chromium against four routes reachable with no session. Executed on this machine 2026-09-16: 18 mutations installed, 18 killed, 0 survived, baseline green, byte-identical restore, green again. THREE OF THESE MUTATIONS SURVIVED EARLIER RUNS, and each survivor found a different boundary — which is the most useful thing this battery has produced. (1) M3 (`<SswField />`) and M4 (`<ManualSelect />`) survived because the guard read the page ONCE, after load, and /master is a FIVE-STEP wizard whose labels it was measuring 23 of 90. The guard was not blind, it was SCOPE-LIMITED, and it reported a confident 100% for the 26% it happened to look at. The sweep now advances the wizard and ASSERTS the step count (M13 makes Next a no-op to prove that assertion can fail), and M3/M4 are the regression test for it. (2) M15 (the education `Tambah` becomes a no-op) survived the NEXT run, because the growth check was AGGREGATE: step 3 has two loops, so clicking every `+` and comparing the screen total is satisfied by whichever loop still works (measured: education delta 0, job delta 6, screen total 12 -> 18, guard green). The check is now PER BUTTON, and M15/M16 kill the two buttons on that screen individually — M15 alone cannot distinguish a walk over all buttons from a walk that only ever looks at #0. (3) M18 pins the group assertion: the `<legend>` is emptied, so the block renders, nothing is logged, and the group silently has no accessible name — invisible both to a source-level check and to the unassociated-label check, because no `<label>` is involved. M10 is the anti-vacuity control: it turns every label on /siswa-baru into a <span>, so the zero-label guard must fire. CAVEAT recorded rather than hidden: the row expansion adds exactly ONE extra row per loop, so a defect that only appears at three rows or more (or only on the first row) is still not covered by any mutation here. The 95 remaining `noLabelWithoutControl` locations are all in admin modals and are NOT measured by this guard; of those, 80 are followed by a control and 15 are not (group labels, a label above a <button>, a <label> used as a heading) — see docs/UI_DESIGN_REVIEW.md §27.9.
